column1: What is a token, as used by inference providers?
column2: The smallest unit a language model deals with — a subword piece produced by a tokenizer, from a vocabulary of around 100,000 units.

column1: How many characters is one English token, roughly?
column2: Roughly four characters, or three quarters of a word.

column1: Why are output tokens more expensive to produce than input tokens?
column2: Output requires running the full forward pass token by token; input is processed in a single parallel prefill pass.

column1: What are the three objects the chapter says travel on the fifth wire?
column2: Tokens, embeddings, and structured calls (function/tool calls conforming to JSON schemas).

column1: What physical transport layer does the AI API wire run on?
column2: Standard TCP/HTTPS/HTTP2-or-3 and JSON — no new physical layer is required.
